span.label: how the cortical representation of a sound changes when the sound is repeatedly heard and means nothing, and changes again when the same sound becomes useful
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: what happens to auditory cortical representations over days of passive experience, which has been hard to ask because the same cells could not be followed that long

span.label: passive daily exposure suppresses pyramidal responses and recruits inhibition through SOM cells, and task engagement reverses it by suppressing those same SOM cells

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repeated passive exposure raises SOM interneuron activity, and the added SOM-mediated inhibition suppresses layer 2/3 pyramidal responses to the experienced tone.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Task engagement suppresses SOM cell firing, releasing pyramidal cells from local inhibition and thereby enlarging the representation of the behaviorally relevant sound.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: habituation is an active process that recruits inhibition rather than a simple withdrawal of excitation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SOM cells are the source, since their tone-evoked excitation grows with the same experience that suppresses everything else
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV cells cannot be the source because their excitation falls with experience like the pyramidal cells they would have to inhibit
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the enhancement is specific to the sustained part of the response, matching where the suppression of pyramidal activity is strongest
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: sound-guided behavior had the opposite effect on SOM cells compared to L2/3 pyramidal cells, with fewer SOM cells excited by the tone during the behaving block
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: filtering sustained sounds while preserving onsets is proposed as the function, since onsets carry the more urgent information
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Spike inference from calcium signals is sensitivity-limited, so conclusions were re-checked on raw dF/F.
span.note: what this limits: the spike-inference analyses, with the check stated: ALTHOUGH DATA ANALYSES USING SPIKE INFERENCE CAN BE AFFECTED BY SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIO, OUR CONCLUSIONS WERE IDENTICAL WHEN DF/F VALUES WERE USED

span.label: Residual neuropil contamination of cellular signals cannot be excluded.
span.note: what this limits: the single-cell specificity of the signals: WE CANNOT EXCLUDE SOME RESIDUAL CONTAMINATION OF CELLULAR SIGNALS BY NEUROPIL RESPONSES, though the conclusions do not depend on the degree of background subtraction
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The use of prolonged tones and a sound-offset detection task may itself explain the divergence from earlier task-engagement studies.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison with the earlier task literature: the use of prolonged tones and a sound-offset detection task may itself explain the divergence

span.label: Other mechanisms contributing to auditory habituation are not excluded.
span.note: what this limits: the sufficiency of the SOM account: WE DO NOT EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY THAT OTHER MECHANISMS COULD CONTRIBUTE TO AUDITORY HABITUATION UNDER DIFFERENT CONDITIONS

span.label: PV cell excitation after habituation is too sparse for a fine comparison during behaviour

span.label: the use of prolonged tones and an offset detection task may itself account for differences from earlier task-engagement studies that used transient sounds

span.label: the effect of silencing shrank when the same experiment was repeated over days, which is read as compensation downstream

Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN DESCRIBES A WITHDRAWAL OF EXCITATION, AND THE EDGE RECORDS A CAUSE OF IT) · habituation —causes→ excitation
span.note: RETRACTED: THE SPAN DESCRIBES A WITHDRAWAL OF EXCITATION, AND THE EDGE RECORDS A CAUSE OF IT. 'habituation in A1 is NOT JUST A SIMPLE WITHDRAWAL OF EXCITATION; rather it ALSO REFLECTS A PRONOUNCED INCREASE IN INHIBITORY RESPONSES.' Habituation REDUCES excitation and adds inhibition; `habituation --causes--> excitation` inverts both halves of the sentence. And `reflects` is an indexing verb, not a causal one - the third vocabulary gap arriving as a mis-type. — strength of the relation: 1 — habituation is an active recruitment of inhibition rather than a withdrawal of excitation, and it filters out what lacks behavioral relevance
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: habituation —causes→ inhibition
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 1 — twenty minutes a day for five days, and the whole effect is carried by a rise in inhibition
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TRF —distinct-from→ excitation

span.label: dF/F —distinct-from→ neuropil
